messages.subject: N vs Nb
parts:
Hello

=20

I am running some analyses where the bootstrap N (Nb) is sometimes up to =
twice as large as the simple N estimate. I understand that Nb is the =
mean of all the bootstrap re-samplings. But I am not clear about what =
circumstances would lead to such a large difference between N and Nb. It =
seems to me that they should be similar. I am also not clear about which =
one is more appropriate for use under these circumstances.

=20

Any help appreciated!

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: N vs Nb
parts:
On Mon, 19 Jun 2006, Daniel Pike wrote:

> > I am running some analyses where the bootstrap N (Nb) is sometimes up
> > to twice as large as the simple N estimate. I understand that Nb is the
> > mean of all the bootstrap re-samplings. But I am not clear about what
> > circumstances would lead to such a large difference between N and Nb. It
> > seems to me that they should be similar. I am also not clear about which
> > one is more appropriate for use under these circumstances.

Daniel, Distance outputs the man bootstrap estimate on the bootstrap
summary page. If individual bootstrap estimates are up to double the
original estimate, this isn't a problem, though it indicates high
variance. If the mean is double the original estimate, then that is a
problem. You shouldn't use the bootstrap estimate, though it can be used
to correct the original estimate for bias. I don't do this because the
bias adjustment can have very high variance, so it can make your estimate
worse in terms of root mean square error. In your case, the bias-adjusted
estimate is likely to be too small - possibly even negative!

I don't know why you're getting this ... possibly you have too few lines
to make reliable use of the bootstrap, and a high proportion of your
detections are from a single line? I would not use the bootstrap if you
have less than around 12 lines, and I would prefer at least 20. If most
of your detections are from just 2 or 3 lines, again I would not use the
bootstrap. The nonparametric bootstrap performs very badly if you
have small numbers of lines or your detections are concentrated on a
small proportion of lines.

Steve
